text: You're flat on your back. The Teqqellon has shifted over your lower half — its teal membrane pressing cold and heavy across your hips and thighs. Its lilac core pulses a few inches above your stomach, the lobes slow and deliberate. It doesn't squeeze. It waits.

options.text: > Press your palms against it and push

text: You stop moving. The membrane responds to the lack of resistance — it presses closer, a slow increase in weight, its surface weeping thin fluid along your skin. Your hands rest at your sides. The core drifts lower. You feel a faint chemical sting at your inner thigh, numbing and shallow. Then it stills again, reading your heat.

You press your palms flat against the teal surface and push. It gives — then flows back. No grip, no resistance, no reaction. Your arms sink slightly into the membrane. You stop pushing. It settles over you again, warmer than before.

After a long still moment, its core dims. The membrane draws back in segments, peeling from your skin with a faint wet sound and pulling its mass inward. It settles into a low, compact heap nearby — core dark, barely pulsing. You sit up.
